key_insight: Unforced DSMC simulations connect intrinsic finite-particle fluctuations to data-extracted second-mode instability dynamics in a hypersonic boundary layer.
engineering_relevance: This approach could support hypersonic transition prediction by relating a measurable numerical disturbance floor to boundary-layer instability rather than prescribing disturbance spectra.
method: Simulate Mach 6 nitrogen over a 120 mm flat plate using DSMC with no imposed disturbances.
Vary particle count to control the finite-particle noise floor while preserving the time-averaged flow.
Extract frequencies, growth rates, and spatial structures with DMD; compare them with LST second-mode expectations.
evidence_signal: DMD analysis of unforced DSMC snapshots yields instability characteristics that are assessed against the second-mode band predicted by linear stability theory.
watch_item: Finite-particle noise is a numerical disturbance source; its equivalence to physical flight or experimental disturbances requires further validation.
paper_title: DSMC Study of Hypersonic Boundary-Layer Unsteadiness Using Data-Driven Analysis
